rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline meant to finish the course and gather telemetry. Geometry: five line sensors spread across 0.06 m at the front of the body (y=0.05 m ahead of the axle), 12 mm footprint so the 25 mm tape always covers at least one or two sensors. Weights are antisymmetric and scale with sensor position (-1.0 to +1.0), so a left-of-centre tape gives a positive signal that steers left, as the contract requires. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn rate and speed; mass 0.8 kg keeps yaw inertia modest. Controller: base_speed 1.6 (about 80% PWM) to aim for the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in under 3 s; kp 4.0 gives a strong but not violent correction (a full-scale signal gives about 1400 PWM of differential); ki 0.1 is small to avoid integral windup on bends; kd 0.2 damps oscillation with little noise amplification; line_loss 'last_direction' lets the robot recover toward the side it was last on. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some wobble on the slalom. I expect rms_error to be a few millimetres and line_loss_events near zero. The first race should show whether speed or kp is the limit. Hypotheses to test: (1) finish time is limited by base_speed, not steering; (2) kp 4 is enough without kd-induced jitter; (3) the 0.06 m outer sensors are not needed on gentle bends.
